about: What a bus terminal's ticket seller knows: what each city is known for, and how long the trip takes from here (typical first-class bus time, rounded).

cities.ciudad-de-mexico: tacos al pastor off the trompo, and the Zócalo with its cathedral
cities.oaxaca: the land of seven moles, mezcal sipped slowly, and the Guelaguetza in July
cities.guadalajara: torta ahogada and birria, and tequila with mariachis in the plazas
cities.san-miguel-de-allende: the Parroquia over the Jardín, and the evening paseo with mariachis
cities.puebla: mole poblano, born here by legend in a convent kitchen, and blue-and-white Talavera

trips.ciudad-de-mexico|guadalajara: about 7 h by ETN or Primera Plus, or about 1 h 15 by plane
trips.ciudad-de-mexico|oaxaca: about 6 h to 6 h 30 by ADO
trips.ciudad-de-mexico|puebla: about 2 h to 2 h 30 by ADO
trips.ciudad-de-mexico|san-miguel-de-allende: about 3 h 30 to 4 h by Primera Plus or ETN
trips.guadalajara|oaxaca: about 1 h 30 by plane, or a long night on the bus (about 13 to 15 h) via Mexico City
trips.guadalajara|puebla: about 9 to 10 h by bus, or about 1 h 30 by plane
trips.guadalajara|san-miguel-de-allende: about 5 to 6 h by Primera Plus or ETN, sometimes changing in León or Querétaro
trips.oaxaca|puebla: about 4 h 30 to 5 h by ADO
trips.oaxaca|san-miguel-de-allende: a long day by bus: about 10 to 11 h, changing in Mexico City or Querétaro
trips.puebla|san-miguel-de-allende: about 5 to 6 h by bus, sometimes changing in Querétaro or Mexico City
